pf.license.need: if: a roofing license or registration for the company, where the state's form requires one (some states license roofing on its own, some under a contractor or home improvement license, some not at all)
ask: The company's roofing license or registration number, and its class
Any job-size limit the license has
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
A bond, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.holder: The business; plus a qualifying person where the state's form names one. Solar installers hold their own licenses where the state asks.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
blocks: No roofing goes live until the company's license checks out, where one is required
A job over the license's size limit is never offered or quoted: the owner is told why
pf.license.declared_emergency: In a declared emergency, the owner says which licenses in that area have lapsed, and a roofer new to the state is held until the owner says yes, where the state's rules say so
pf.license.renewals: License, insurance and bond dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses new bookings
pf.license.lead_safe: Work that disturbs painted trim or fascia on older homes only by a firm and a person certified for lead-safe work, where the rules require it
pf.license.showroom: The showroom: a registration, and a seller's license for each consultant who sells roof work, only where the state's form asks
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks

pf.services.pattern: Inspection, then project: a roof is booked only after a written estimate and a signed contract

pf.services.capacity: One estimator or consultant per booking; 1 roof per crew per day, up to 30 squares; the showroom's layout table is saved with long sessions
pf.services.skills: Inspections and estimates: estimators. Installs: crew leads with their crews. Solar: licensed installers. Showroom: consultants.
pf.services.nobody_home: Roof work outside: nobody needs to be home; a start photo and day-end photos. An adult is needed only for the attic check at the inspection.
pf.services.online: No video consult: shingle picks use the samples at the showroom

before_times: What's wrong: storm damage, a leak, or an old roof?
Roof type: shingle, tile, metal or flat
About how old is the roof?
How many stories is the house?
after_time: Have you filed an insurance claim? Yes or no only, never the claim's details
The year the home was built (painted trim on older homes may need lead-safe work, where the rules require it)
OK to go on the roof and take photos?
Will an adult be home for a 5-minute attic check?
Do you own the home or rent? (the owner signs any contract)
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the home, or someone with the owner's written OK. Everyone on the home's title signs a roof contract.
showroom: Which part of the house: the roof, skylights or trim
Photos of the house, and an old tile or shingle if there is one (optional)

stop.words: a tree through the roof or a wall, power lines down on or near the house
stop.says: Leave the house and stay far from the lines. Then call 911 and the power company.
stop.booking: no booking until the house is safe

stop.words: a ceiling sagging, bulging or falling
stop.says: Get everyone out of that room, and call 911 if anyone is at risk.

stop.words: a gas smell, sparking or smoking wires
stop.says: Leave the house now. Then call 911 and the gas or power company.

steps_then_go_on.words: water dripping inside, a wet or stained ceiling
steps_then_go_on.says: Keep everyone out from under it, and catch the drips in a bucket. Turn that room off at the breaker only if it's safe to reach. Don't go on the roof.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on, marked urgent; the emergency tarp is offered first, with Sam's OK

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether a roof is safe to walk on, or about the structure, go to the business's own line
pf.safety.never: Customers are told never to climb on a damaged or wet roof

pf.first_steps.before_quote: The inspection at the home: the roof and the attic, photos by slope, squares measured
after_contract: The cancel window ends before any work or orders, where the state's rules give one
The permit, pulled by the license holder in the business's name, and any notice the state's rules require before work starts
Shingles and a dumpster delivered the day before the install
A dry forecast the day before the tear-off
prep: An adult home for the 5-minute attic check at the inspection
Before the install: move cars from the driveway, take pictures off the walls, and keep pets inside
showroom_prep: Bring an old tile or shingle, if there is one
pf.first_steps.sample_pickup: A 15-minute sample pickup before a full exterior plan, at least 2 days before, so the shingles are seen on the house in daylight

pf.visit.check_in: Inspection: the check-in code at the door, with an adult home for the attic. Install day: nobody needs to be home; the crew texts a start photo. Showroom: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The roof is walked only when it's dry. Photos by slope, an attic look, squares measured. The written report and estimate come the same day, good for 30 days. Nothing is signed or paid at the inspection.
pf.visit.wet_roof: Never walk a wet roof: inspect by drone and from the attic, or move the time
pf.visit.changes: Rotted decking at the contract's price per sheet, up to the count OK'd in the contract, with photos and a change order for the record. Past it, a signed change order before that work.
pf.visit.install_day: Plants and the AC unit covered; the roof sealed the same day; a magnet sweep of the yard, driveway and street for nails, with photos; day-end photos to the customer
pf.visit.outside_checks: The city's final inspection, where the permit requires it
pf.visit.done: The final inspection where needed, then the walk-around and nail sweep, then DONE
pf.visit.showroom_done: DONE after the consult, with the picks saved for the inspection and estimate
pf.visit.before_photos: Each slope of the roof, the attic and any ceiling stains

pf.money.inspection: The example's $89 inspection counts toward the roof work, and is billed only if no contract follows. A free inspection is a safe start.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On a new roof, nothing is taken before the contract is signed by everyone
pf.money.deposit: Only after signing; the deposit cap comes from the state's form
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart or bonded where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.balance: After the city's final inspection; never ahead of the work
pf.money.insurance: The customer's own insurance claim pays the customer, never through Rosie or the business. The deductible is always the customer's: never paid, waived or rebated.
pf.money.insurance_check: If the balance waits for the insurer's check, Sam picks: wait, or call
pf.money.storm_prices: In a declared emergency, prices stay at the list from before it, for as long as the state's rules say
pf.money.rosfield_fee: Rosfield's $2 can be switched off by state and by who pays, where a state's rule on pay for referrals reaches it (a switch from the state's form, for counsel to confirm)
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe, for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check also works: the crew lead texts 'paid check'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on materials and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.showroom: The roof preview session's $55 counts toward the roof if Alex signs with Lee Roofing; the $20 missed-consult fee only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: Contract, change order and permit papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home never lets the crew in, and never goes in the attic with them
pf.messages.no_claim_ads: No text ever urges anyone to file an insurance claim

pf.staff.roles: Estimators and crew leads (Diego, Owen): inspections, estimates, and installs with their crews. Showroom consultants (Hana, Ruby).
pf.staff.licenses: The company holds the roofing license; solar installers hold their own, checked before they're named on a job
pf.staff.drone: Drone inspections only by a pilot who holds the federal remote pilot certificate
pf.staff.lead_safe: A certified renovator on any job that disturbs painted trim on an older home, where lead-safe rules apply
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes and change orders over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another estimator may take an inspection; an install keeps its crew lead unless Sam moves it
pf.staff.on_call: Emergency tarps: Diego weeknights, Owen weekends, each the other's backup

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for a new roof where the state's rules require one, signed by everyone on title and by the business before any money
pf.rules.contract_parts: The parts the state's form lists (license number, price, dates, deposit, cancel notice, any lien or recovery-fund notice, who owes the deductible)
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; a longer one for contracts signed in a declared emergency, where the rules say so. Work and orders wait for it.
pf.rules.claim_denied: A contract signed before the insurer decides: any right to cancel after a written denial, where the state's rules give one
pf.rules.insurance_claims: The business never files, adjusts or explains the customer's claim, unless the state's rules allow it; no gifts or rebates tied to an inspection or a claim
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the license holder in the business's name, never the homeowner's
pf.rules.notice_before_work: Any notice the state's rules require before work starts, filed by the owner of the business
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before added work, past what the contract already OK'd
pf.rules.final: The city's final inspection before the balance is asked for
pf.rules.lien_release: A lien release with the final payment, where the state's rules provide one
pf.rules.show: The license number on the listing, the times read out, the confirmation, the estimate, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.storm_prices: Prices from before a declared emergency, for as long as the state's rules say
pf.rules.warranty: 10 years on a new roof's workmanship and 1 year on repairs (the example's); the shingle maker's warranty registered in the owner's name

pf.edges.weather: No tear-off at a 40% chance of rain or more (the example business's own limit); a weather move never costs the customer
pf.edges.wet_roof: Rain at inspection time: a drone and attic look, or a new time
pf.edges.leak_gets_worse: Safety steps first, then the emergency tarp offered with Sam's OK and a written price
pf.edges.hidden_damage: Rotted decking: at the contract's price per sheet, inside the count OK'd; past it, a signed change order first
pf.edges.insurance_wait: The estimate waits on the customer's insurer until its good-until date, with one reminder
pf.edges.insurance_check: The balance may wait for the insurer's check: Sam picks wait or call
pf.edges.deductible_offer: A customer or a door-knocker offers a deductible deal: answered with the plug-in's rule, never paid, waived or rebated
pf.edges.declared_emergency: The owner says which licenses lapsed, newcomers held until the owner says yes, storm-period contracts marked, prices from before it
pf.edges.permit_late: The install moves with no fee; the customer is told
pf.edges.inspection_fails: The crew fixes it and it's checked again; the balance waits
pf.edges.nobody_home: Install days: start and day-end photos
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

Diego inspects it Thu Oct 22 between 8 and 10am and sends a written estimate. Once Alex's insurer and Alex say yes, the crew puts on a new roof. The money choice you pick changes the path.

notes:
Pilot: contractor (from: contractor). A roofer runs like a remodeler: an inspection at the home first, then a written estimate, a contract signed by everyone on title, a deposit, a cancel window, a permit, the work, an outside inspection, then the last bill. Only the timing differs: one install day instead of weeks, and no stage bills between the deposit and the balance.
Flow B (main path visit|none|bill): a storm-damaged roof at 58 Cedar Ln. The booking is the $89 roof inspection, priced at the visit. Diego's report and written estimate ($14,800: 24 squares at $575, $650 permit and dumpster, $350 ridge vent and vent boots) are B8-20's words. The '1 Signs the contract' branch (the master's 'An estimate becomes its own job', renamed) holds the insurance question (B8-x01 to B8-x04), the contract (B8-62), the $1,000 deposit (B8-63), the cancel window (B8-x05, B8-x06) and the permit (B8-x07, B8-x08).
The install runs on B8-22's 'The job runs several days': B8-37 carries the install plan, then the own steps for the forecast before the tear-off (B8-x09, B8-x10), the start photo (B8-x11), the rotted decking (B8-x12, B8-x13) and the day-end photos and nail sweep (B8-x14). The city's final inspection is B8-65/B8-50/B8-51 (words). The balance, $14,370 ($14,800 less the $1,000 deposit, plus the $570 decking change order), is the last bill (B9-05 to B9-26 words). Receipt $15,370 with the lien release and both warranties (B10-01).
The example inspection costs $89 (the master's number, so its holds and fees stay true), counted toward the roof work if Alex signs. The old flowchart's inspection was free; the plug-in says a free inspection is the safe start.
Insurance: the customer's own claim is Alex's to file and handle; Rosie asks only how he will pay (B8-x01). The estimate waits for the insurer until its good-until date (B8-x02); a denial keeps it open (B8-x03); a deductible deal is refused (B8-x04). The insurer's money goes to Alex, never through Rosie. Raised as a general gap.
Rotted decking is OK'd in the contract up to 10 sheets at $95 each, so the crew never stops with the roof open (change order 1 is for the record); an 11th sheet needs a signed change order (B8-x13). Raised as a general gap (extra work pre-approved up to a limit).
B8-20's '1 Yes, fix it' and '3 OK some lines' are off: nothing is done or signed at a roof inspection, and a roof estimate is signed whole. A small repair is its own written quote (B8-27, B8-28). '2 Not today' keeps the master's path (only the $89 is owed, the report is Alex's). 'No answer: Alex is out' is renamed 'No reply in 7 days' (the old flowchart's 7 days), with one reminder, then Sam (B8-49 words).
B10-29's 'A permit: the city inspects' is off: the final inspection runs during the job (B8-50), and the balance waits for it.
Weather: the old business's limit (no tear-off at a 40% chance of rain or more) is the example's own, in pf.edges; a weather move never costs the customer. A wet roof is never walked: an inspection uses a drone and the attic, or a new time (B7-35 more; drone pilots hold the federal remote pilot certificate, pf.staff).
Every state rule is a switch from the state's form: the license and its job-size limit, the written contract and its parts, the deposit cap, money kept apart, the cancel window (longer for contracts signed in a declared emergency where the rules say so), cancel after an insurer's written denial, permits and notices before work, lien releases, no deductible deals or claim handling, prices in a declared emergency. The old flowchart's Florida, California, Missouri, Pennsylvania, New York and Texas rules and numbers are dropped (180 days, 10 days, 10% or $1,000, $2,500, 5 business days, pre-1978).
Lead-safe work is written as 'painted trim on older homes, where the rules require it'; the year the home was built is asked after a time is saved, with no cutoff year from one law.
The old flowchart's AccuLynx, JobNimbus, ServiceTitan, Roofr and Leap parts are OUTDATED: Rosie is the software now.
Second kind of work: solar (trade name Lee Solar), which waits for its installer's own license where the state asks (the master's electrical). Second company: Lee Exterior Showroom (the master's Lee's Barbershop), where customers come in to pick shingles, skylights and trim.
Flow A (main path list|card|counter): a $35 shingle consult with Hana at the showroom, a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee, paid at the showroom desk. A8-x01 offers Diego's inspection at home, which runs in flow B. Showroom services keep the barbershop's prices: shingle consult $35, skylight pick $40, sample kit $20, trim match $25, roof preview session $55 (credited to the roof), full exterior plan $140, metal roof plan from photos ($90), tile roof match after a $25 consult. A patch test becomes a 15-minute sample pickup.
Off in A: the child branches (A4-24, A8-32), and the repeat-plan branches (A4-28, A5-01, A7-02): a showroom sells no plan of consults. Flow B keeps its plans (a yearly moss treatment, Morgan's roof check at two rentals).
Plug-in splits: every one is decided. Off where the roofer never uses a branch (spaces, classes, seats, stays, a set start, no person named, a damage hold, a delivery to sign for, items leaving the home, a date that can't move, the child in the pro's care, no $2, no license). splitsKept for the ones it uses branch by branch: A7-61 (a stand-in for a consult, none for a tile match), A8-02 (an old tile to bring for a match), B4-81, B7-55, B8-58 (the emergency tarp is sent now, an inspection never), B4-57 (a skylight over the plug-in's amount takes a contract, a shingle repair none), B8-69, B8-70 (roof work needs nobody home, the inspection's attic check needs an adult), B8-65 (a new roof has the city's final inspection, a repair none).
B8-72 '1 An item goes to the workshop' and B10-07 'The chimney cap isn't taken back' are off: nothing of the customer's leaves the home on roof work. Their rename (a copper chimney cap to the workshop) stays only so the master's words read right where they're shown off.
Money combinations used: B visit|none|bill, visit|none|own, visit|hold|bill, list|hold|bill (a $179 shingle repair with the $89 held), photos|deposit|bill (a $640 skylight from photos, a contract, a $160 deposit). A list|card|counter, list|none|counter, list|full|none, list|deposit|counter. Left out: the saved card charged at DONE on a roof (big bills are paid by link, bank transfer or check) and paid-in-full roofs.
Rosfield's $2 for the roof booking comes out of the deposit, once (B8-63, B9-07). The old flowchart's 'no fee on Florida roof jobs' is a gap (the $2 switched by who pays), not a rule here.
Names: Jordan and Casey are Diego and Owen (estimators and crew leads); Riley and Avery are Hana and Ruby (showroom consultants); Theo B. is Nico B. Addresses: 58 Cedar Ln (Alex), 310 Quarry Rd (the showroom), 460 Depot St (Lee Roofing). License numbers renamed (RC, SC, SR, SP, RF, SE). Kim's outdoor job is a shingle repair; Rosa's call is a roof leak into a bedroom.
The master's plumbing jobs keep their prices as the example's own: shingle repair $179 (drain clearing), moss treatment $150 (water heater flush), skylight replacement $640 from photos (water heater replacement), roof repair at the visit $245 with flashing $165 and shingle work $80 (leak repair), roof certification $199 (sewer camera), cracked vent boots $160 and a vent cap $95 as extras.
keep: roofing, roofer and leak. They are the profession's own words (the contractor pilot used roofing as its second kind of work; a roof leak is the roofer's core job).
Pipe boots are written 'vent boots' so no plumbing word ('pipe') is left in the flows.
The joined reading was done with prof-read.js (work/prof/roofer-read-A.md and -read-B.md) and a scratch path reader: sections 3-10 of both main paths, the other combinations' changed steps, and sections 1-2 and 11-13 skimmed.
Review (Oct 22): added the money paths the plug-in itself names: A list|hold|counter (full exterior plan, $40 held), photos|card|counter (metal roof plan), visit|card|counter (tile roof match); B list|none|bill (the emergency tarp and a returning customer's shingle repair), list|full|none and list|deposit|bill (moss treatment). Fixed leftover words: S1-60/S2-28 'barbering' (now as the plug-in says: roofing licenses the company, solar and showroom sales each person, so Owen isn't checked), A4-50 'About an inch.', A4-22/A6-15 'Short on the sides.' and 'brassy', A7-38 'steamer', B8-27/B8-28 'main water line' on the photos path. The inspection booking reads 'Roof inspection', not 'Roof repair', on the booking cards (B3-04, B4-29, B5-03, B6-04, B6-13, B6-14, B7-01). Off in A: the plan and insurance branches (A4-28, A4-54, A7-02, A9-15). A8-34 on the tile-match path no longer says a "custom plan-correction session".
touch-up 4 (Oct 23): B8-39's base line (the $179 shingle repair paths) still had the plumber's 'runs the water with Alex and checks for drips'; the B8-39 words op now says Diego and Alex look over the shingle repair together. Keep 'drips': water that drips through a ceiling, catching the drips, and a skylight that drips at one corner are real roofing words.
